title: Pulse Rotary: Ops Playbook & Shift Synthesis (Oct 04 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the ops synthesis from the Oct 4 shift rotation: incident recap, SLO snapshot, handoff checklist adjustments, and short-term action items. Intended audience: SRE rotation leads, infra eng, serving-runtime owners, and product incident reviewers.

Summary (TL;DR):
- A region-wide tail-latency spike affected eu-west-1 between 2027-10-03 22:40 UTC and 2027-10-04 01:05 UTC. Total user-facing error rate was low (<0.15%), but 95th/99th token-latencies exceeded SLOs for 2.5 hours during peak traffic patterns.
- Primary trigger: aggressive KV-cache eviction after a config rollback plus an inadvertent model-variant fallback routing that amplified CPU/GPU context thrash.
- Mitigation: emergency rollback of the eviction policy at 22:55 UTC, temporary routing throttle to dedicated capacity pools at 23:12 UTC, and an autoscaler tuning patch deployed 00:08 UTC.
- Impact: SLO (per-region p99 < 1200ms for generation API) breached in eu-west for a 2.5-hour window. No data loss or security issues.

Incident timeline (concise):
- 22:31 UTC: First latency alerts (p95 > 700ms) from eu-west dashboards; on-call page routed to SRE-ops primary.
- 22:36 UTC: Rapid spike to p99 ~ 2200ms; paging escalated.
- 22:40 UTC: Initial triage — observed high KV-cache miss rate and frequent small-batch kernel launches on GPUs (inefficient).
- 22:48 UTC: Team hypothesis — recent rollback of cache-eviction tuning (Config ID: cfg-evict-2027-09-21) may have been re-applied by automation job srep/auto-config-apply.
- 22:55 UTC: Manual override: re-apply conservative eviction thresholds and flush stale cache entries on affected nodes. Latency improved but not back to baseline.
- 23:12 UTC: Observed that traffic routing was falling back to a cheaper model-variant (quantized) due to capacity pressure; those variants triggered heavier CPU-side preprocessing. Enabled routing throttle to keep requests on standard variants while scaling.
- 00:08 UTC: Autoscaler tuning patch (PR #468) deployed: increased GPU headroom and extended cooldown to avoid oscillation.
- 00:27 UTC: Metrics show steady improvement; p99 trending below 900ms.
- 01:05 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; on-call debrief scheduled for Oct 05.

Root cause analysis (working):
- Contributing factors:
  1) Automation re-applied an older eviction config during a cross-service config sync. There is no safe-guard preventing eviction changes during high-traffic windows.
  2) Fallback routing logic prioritized model-variant compatibility over runtime cost, causing unexpected CPU preprocessing when quantized variants were used under load.
  3) Autoscaler cooldown parameters were too short, which allowed oscillations when pods/nodes recycled and temporarily reduced capacity.
- Primary root cause (probable): conflict between config-sync automation and runtime-serving heuristics that combined to create sustained cache thrash and variant-driven CPU pressure.

SLO snapshot (post-incident rounding):
- Generation API (global): SLO p99 < 1200ms, target 99.95%
- eu-west-1: observed window where p99 = 2200ms for ~2.5 hours. Estimated SLO burn: ~0.7% of monthly budget for that region.
- Error budget implications: actionable for region-specific rollouts; consider throttling non-critical experiments in eu-west until fixes are enacted.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- [Ava] Create temporary config-lock on eviction policies for high-traffic windows (safety flag): ETA 2027-10-06.
- [Diego] Add explicit guard to the config-syncer to ignore eviction-related keys unless manual approval present: ETA 2027-10-11.
- [Priya] Adjust fallback routing policy to account for CPU preprocessing cost metric (add weight to CPU in decision function): ETA 2027-10-14.
- [Samir] Harden autoscaler cooldown defaults for GPU pools; add noise buffer to avoid synchronized churn: ETA 2027-10-08.
- [Runbook] Update generation-api runbook with a new KV-cache triage checklist and quick rollback snippet: ETA 2027-10-07 (owner: shift lead).

Runbook changes (proposed snippets):
- Add step: "If p95 > 700ms and KV-cache-miss-rate > 15% then set eviction.policy=conservative and trigger cache-flush for affected nodes".
- Add quick-check command examples for quick correlation:
  - galaxy metrics query: metrics/query?m=kv_miss_rate{region=eu-west-1}&range=15m
  - routing check: /api/route/debug?route=generation&window=10m

Handoff checklist (new additions):
- Confirm config-lock status in config-syncer dashboard.
- Verify fallback routing weights (CPU vs latency) show no negatives for primary variants.
- Confirm autoscaler cooldown is set to >= 5m for GPU pools for the next 48 hours.
- Attach incident slack thread and postmortem link into the next handoff note.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did the automation job re-apply an older eviction config without a change event? Need audit logs traced to srep/auto-config-apply run history.
- Are there precursors in workload patterns (prompt length distribution changes) that made cache eviction more sensitive this week? (Data team follow-up).

Planned follow-ups (longer-term):
- Policy: stop any eviction/GC-related automated config changes during region-wide peak windows — require two-person approval. (Policy draft by 2027-10-20).
- Experiment: deploy simulated cache-thrash load tests to validate autoscaler behavior and routing fallback under synthetic worst-case sequences. (Infra + serving-runtime).
- Telemetry: add a composite signal that combines kv_miss_rate, small-batch kernel launches, and CPU-queue length to preemptively trigger protective routing.

Notes for next shift lead (practical):
- If you see p99 rising but p50 stable, check KV miss rate and small-batch kernel events first before scaling horizontally. Scaling may exacerbate oscillation if eviction is misconfigured.
- Use the temporary routing throttle (operations -> routing -> throttle) if you observe quantized variants spiking CPU preproc.

Debrief meeting invite:
- Scheduled: 2027-10-05 16:00 UTC (SRE postmortem sync). Full agenda will be added to the confluence page.

Appendix (quick links):
